extraction_method: Manual transcription of published figures/tables only; no raw sample records or personal data.

sources.title: State control and monitoring trends of drinking water quality in Georgia
sources.review_status: Formal peer-review procedure for this article was not independently verified from accessible journal policy pages.

sources.title: Summary reports in accordance with article 7 of the Protocol on Water and Health — Georgia

unece_context.interpretation: The narrative and E. coli table have different indicator contexts. The equal 2024 value does not prove that the indicators are identical.

cross_source_context.comparability: unresolved; no common sample frame, denominator or indicator crosswalk is supplied

limitations: Published figures are transcribed aggregates, not raw sample-level observations.
JECM 2020 and 2021 national and regional sample counts do not reconcile.
The JECM article does not provide raw data or a complete sample-level denominator and selection design.
The UNECE/WHO report does not provide sample denominators or urban/rural E. coli values in the cited table.
No causal, temporal trend, municipal ranking or current water-safety conclusion is supported by these aggregates.

table1_violation_category_counts.category_count_semantics: Table 1 contains combined violation categories in all four years. The authors explicitly state that microbiological and organoleptic violations coexisted in the same sample in 2020 and that several combinations coexisted in 2023 (p.5); the table itself lists combined categories in 2021-2022 as well. These are violation-type frequencies, not unique-sample counts. Category-frequency shares must not be interpreted as sample-level prevalence.
